kept.title: NoSQL Injection via $where operator
kept.description: The `getByUserIdAndThreshold` method in `app/data/allocations-dao.js` uses unsanitized input within a `$where` clause, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution within the MongoDB engine.
steps_to_exploit: Access the allocations page with a threshold query parameter.
Set the 'threshold' parameter to a string containing a malicious payload like '1) || true //'.
The query executes the payload against the database context.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to database records, potential data exfiltration, or denial of service.

kept.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
kept.description: The `/research` route in `app/routes/research.js` accepts a `url` parameter and performs an outbound HTTP request without validation.
steps_to_exploit: Access /research?url=http://internal-service.local/&symbol=any.
The server performs a GET request to the internal, non-public address.
The response body is returned to the attacker.
kept.impact: Exfiltration of internal network data, port scanning, or interacting with internal APIs behind the firewall.

kept.title: Insecure Password Hashing (Plaintext)
kept.description: User passwords are stored in the database as plaintext instead of using a secure salted hash.
steps_to_exploit: Access the database dump or via a separate SQL/NoSQL injection vulnerability.
Observe the 'password' field in the 'users' collection.
User accounts can be compromised immediately without cracking.
kept.impact: Complete compromise of user credentials upon database access.

kept.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Disabled Autoescaping
kept.description: The Swig templating engine has `autoescape` set to `false`, disabling context-aware output encoding across the application.
steps_to_exploit: Find an input field that is rendered back to the user (e.g., Profile Name).
Inject a payload like '<script>alert(1)</script>'.
The script executes when other users or administrators view the profile.
kept.impact: Session hijacking, credential theft, or unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.

kept.title: Broken Access Control in Benefits
kept.description: The `updateBenefits` method in `app/routes/benefits.js` fails to verify if the requesting user has administrative privileges before modifying data.
steps_to_exploit: Log in as a standard user.
Send a POST request to `/benefits` with `userId` and `benefitStartDate` parameters.
The backend processes the change without checking for the `isAdmin` flag.
kept.impact: Unauthorized modification of sensitive employee benefits data.

kept.description: The admin routes are not consistently protected by the `isAdmin` middleware, exposing administrative functions to regular users.
steps_to_exploit: Access the `/benefits` URL directly while logged in as a normal user.
Verify that the interface allows manipulation of other users' data.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to administrative tools and data.

kept.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via URL parameters
kept.description: The `firstNameSafeString` in `app/views/profile.html` is used in an `href` attribute, allowing malicious URI schemes.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a URL for the profile page with a parameter like '?firstName=javascript:alert(1)'.
A victim clicks the link 'Google search this profile by name'.
The javascript executes.
kept.impact: Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the user's browser session.

kept.title: Insecure Cookie Secret
kept.description: The session management secret is hardcoded in the source code.
steps_to_exploit: Analyze the source code to retrieve the value of `cookieSecret`.
Forge arbitrary session cookies to assume any user identity.
kept.impact: Session hijacking and complete authentication bypass.

kept.title: Information Disclosure via Console Logging
kept.description: The application logs the entire configuration object, including potentially sensitive keys, to the console at startup.
steps_to_exploit: Access the server logs.
Identify the printed configuration object containing sensitive credentials.
kept.impact: Exposure of sensitive environment configurations and secrets.

kept.title: Vulnerable Dependency Usage
kept.description: The package.json includes outdated, vulnerable versions of dependencies (e.g., `swig`, `marked`).
steps_to_exploit: Identify known CVEs associated with the versions listed in `package.json`.
Use public exploit code for these vulnerabilities against the application.
kept.impact: Exposure to known security vulnerabilities in external libraries.

kept.title: Sensitive Information in Source Control
kept.description: Production credentials are hardcoded in test/development configuration files.
steps_to_exploit: Review the git history.
Extract the ZAP API key and other secrets from the repository.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to internal security testing tools and infrastructure.

kept.title: Verbose Error Messages
kept.description: The custom error handler renders the raw error object to the template, potentially revealing stack traces or internal system state.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an application error (e.g., providing malformed input).
Observe the response containing internal error details.
kept.impact: Information disclosure helping attackers map internal system logic.
